title: Query-pair contrastive + recency-weighted reservoir sampler for per-domain calibration packs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a reproducible per-domain calibration-packing algorithm that combines (1) a recency-weighted reservoir sampler to keep packs tuned to live traffic distribution and (2) a query-pair contrastive augmentation step that improves representativeness for response-sensitive quant validation. Output: per-domain calibration packs (fixed-size) plus K-fold holdout splits for accuracy validation across FP8/INT8 profiles.
background: Current calibration packs drift: heavy-tail queries are underrepresented and recent shifts (product launches, seasonal campaigns) aren't captured quickly without huge sample sizes. Existing samplers either over-index on frequency or blindly subsample recent traffic. We also lack a portable augmentation strategy to surface response-level variability important for quantization-induced distributional shifts. This causes false pass/fail signals during offline accuracy validation of quant profiles.
proposed_solution: Build a two-stage pipeline: stage A = recency-weighted reservoir sampler per domain that maintains a fixed-size buffer (N examples) with exponential decay factor alpha controlling age bias; stage B = for each sampled anchor prompt, synthesize 1-3 contrastive query-pairs (paraphrases + minor slot perturbations + negative contextual variants) and include original model responses as canonical references. Stratify the reservoir by domain x response-length bucket to preserve tail-length diversity. Produce deterministic packs via seeded RNG and store metadata (traffic timestamp, tenant-id-hash, fingerprint) for audit and reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Produced per-domain packs of target sizes (e.g., N=10k per domain) with documented seed produce identical output across runs; 2) K-fold holdouts generated and reproducibility tests pass; 3) Offline quant-validation runs (FP8 and INT8) report stable delta metrics (perplexity and token-accuracy proxies) with <5% false alarm rate on historical regressions compared to gold baseline; 4) Sampling pipeline runs <2x cost of current baseline and stores provenance metadata; 5) PR + design review completed and engineering runbook added to Console docs.
experiment_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement reservoir sampler + deterministic seed on small domains (search, summarization) and run FP8/INT8 quant validation on historic 90-day traffic. Phase 2 (augmentation): add paraphrase generator (in-house minimal paraphrase model + rules) and evaluate coverage lift and metric sensitivity. Phase 3 (scale): run across 20 domains, measure distributional coverage, cost, and false-alarm rate. We will run ablation: no-augment vs augment, recency-only vs recency+stratification.
metrics: - Pack coverage: % unique prompt fingerprints vs raw traffic sample. - Recency responsiveness: median timestamp delta of pack items vs last-traffic. - Tail retention: fraction of prompts with response-length > 128 tokens. - Validation stability: regression false-alarm rate on known historical regressions. - Cost: compute + storage per pack. All metrics logged per domain and aggregated.
data_privacy_and_compliance: Store only hashed tenant IDs and optionally redact PII with the existing redact pipeline before pack ingestion. Paraphrase augmentation will operate on redacted text. Maintain an allowlist/denylist for domains with strict retention rules; those domains will use a privacy-mode sampler (no augmentation, TTL < 30 days).
implementation_notes: - Reservoir algorithm: weighted reservoir sampling with weight w = exp(-alpha * age_hours) * (1 + log(freq)) for soft frequency bias. - Stratification: 4 length buckets: <=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512. - Augmentation: lightweight paraphrase model (distilled T5) + deterministic rule-based slot swaps for templated queries. - Provenance: JSONL manifest with fields: fingerprint, ts, seed, domain, length_bucket, aug_flags, quant_profiles_tested. - CI: unit tests for determinism and stochastic tests under fixed RNG seeds.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Aggressive recency bias may underrepresent stable long-tail intents — mitigated by tunable alpha and min-reserve per-length-bucket. - Paraphrase augmentation can introduce artefacts that don't reflect real user language; mitigate by constraining edit distances and by sampling paraphrases only for low-frequency anchors. - Cost: augmentation increases CPU; we'll gate augmentation to low-volume domains or run it offline on spot instances.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flagged rollout - sampler prototype enabled for internal evaluation-only domains. 2) Run offline quant-validation (FP8/INT8) and compare with baseline. 3) Open beta for 5 customer domains with PM/Customer Success oversight. 4) Gradual ramp to all non-restricted domains after 2 successful weeks of stable validation metrics.
notes: This approach is complementary to model-side calibration (per-layer quant calibration). The goal is to reduce dataset-induced false alarms in our accuracy-validation pipelines so quant profile selection is more robust. We'll coordinate with Runtime team for provenance fields and with Console for per-pack visibility.
